Description: Core state machine transition. Validates user role, checks task is actionable, validates required fields from actionMatrix, evaluates json-logic conditions, transitions task (APPROVE/REJECT/REQUEST_INFO). REJECT auto-completes siblings. APPROVE at end step completes instance. Creates next tasks including multireview and join-condition handling.
Authorization: JWT + role-access check via Access Management Service
Criticality Reason: Core workflow engine — every approval/rejection across the entire platform flows through this endpoint. Failure blocks all loan applications, guarantee applications, tenders, claims, PFI onboarding, and MEL reports from progressing. Affects all BRD customers and staff.
Important Log Fields: task_id, instance_id, step_id, action (approve/reject/request_info), actor_user_id, role_code, has_comment, has_file, next_tasks_created_count, instance_completed (bool), namespace, entity_type, entity_ref, duration_ms, trace_id
Sensitive Data: User JWT (contains identificationNumber, autenticatorQrCode, accountToken, phone). Task comments and fileUrl. Staff user emails in notifications.
Dependencies: DB: Heavy transaction — WorkflowTask, WorkflowInstance, WorkflowSchema, WorkflowHistory (multiple CRUD). Kafka via outbox (WorkflowTaskCompleted, WorkflowTaskReady, WorkflowCompleted). HTTP: Authentication Service (staff user lookups for multireview + REQUEST_INFO permission checks). HTTP: Notification Service (email). Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger (console-style). Morgan middleware for HTTP. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Zero distributed tracing. Most complex endpoint in the fleet with no observability. State machine transitions invisible. Join condition evaluation invisible. Multireview fan-out invisible. JSON-logic evaluation invisible.
Notes: Most important endpoint to instrument. 4,444-line service file. Consider adding spans per sub-operation: role validation, json-logic eval, join condition check, next-task creation, notification send.

Description: Starts a new workflow instance. Finds published schema by entity, checks idempotency, creates instance + initial tasks (supports multireview fan-out to multiple users), emits WorkflowStarted + WorkflowTaskReady Kafka events, records START history, sends email notifications.
Criticality Reason: Every approval workflow in the platform begins here. Failure prevents any new loan application, guarantee application, tender, claim, or report from entering the approval pipeline. Direct customer impact.
Important Log Fields: instance_id, schema_id, namespace, entity_type, entity_ref, started_by, idempotency_key, initial_task_count, is_multireview, duration_ms, trace_id
Sensitive Data: User JWT (PII fields). Staff user emails for multireview task assignment.
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowSchema, WorkflowEntity, WorkflowInstance, WorkflowTask, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowStarted, WorkflowTaskReady). HTTP: Authentication Service (getStaffUsers for multireview, getDepartmentByCode/getUnitByCode for labels). HTTP: Notification Service. Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger only. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Zero tracing. Instance creation success/failure rates invisible. Idempotency key collisions invisible. Multireview fan-out invisible.
Notes: Critical path. Idempotency key handling should be logged (new vs existing). Multireview user matching should emit count of matched users.

Description: Cancels an ACTIVE instance. Sets instance status to CANCELLED, cancels all open tasks (READY/CLAIMED/REQUEST_INFO), records history per task + instance, emits WorkflowCancelled, sends cancellation email notifications.
Criticality Reason: Cancelling a workflow cancels an in-progress approval. Affects the underlying business entity (application, tender, etc.). Important but less frequent than start/act. Incorrect cancellations could require manual recovery.
Important Log Fields: instance_id, namespace, entity_ref, cancelled_by, reason, cancelled_task_count, trace_id
Sensitive Data: User JWT. Task assignee IDs. Staff user emails.
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowInstance, WorkflowTask, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowCancelled). HTTP: Authentication Service (staff user lookups). HTTP: Notification Service. Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger only. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Zero tracing. Cancellation reasons not tracked.
Notes: Should track cancellation reasons for business analytics.

Description: Admin force-complete. Iterates all schema steps, creates/completes tasks for each, sets instance COMPLETED. Emits WorkflowTaskCompleted per task + WorkflowCompleted. No additional admin-role check beyond AccessGuard.
Criticality Reason: Admin override of normal workflow — bypasses all approval steps. Security-sensitive: could approve/reject applications without proper review. No additional admin-role verification beyond standard AccessGuard.
Important Log Fields: instance_id, namespace, entity_ref, forced_by, action (approve/reject), tasks_force_completed_count, trace_id
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowSchema, WorkflowInstance, WorkflowTask, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowTaskCompleted, WorkflowCompleted). Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger only. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero observability on admin override actions. Security concern — force-completes bypass normal approval flow with no additional verification or audit trail beyond basic logging.
Notes: Security-critical. Must have prominent domain event + audit trail. Consider whether AccessGuard alone is sufficient or whether an explicit admin-role check should be added. Every force-complete should be highly visible in dashboards.

Description: Resumes a single task from REQUEST_INFO to READY. Validates user has matching requestInfoRoleCode/dept/unit via Authentication Service. Restores task snapshot from history deltaJson. Emits WorkflowTaskReady.
Authorization: JWT + role-access check + additional per-task requestInfo permission check via Authentication Service
Criticality Reason: Resumes a paused approval step. Required for the REQUEST_INFO → READY cycle that unblocks workflows. Failure leaves tasks stuck in REQUEST_INFO state, blocking approvals.
Sensitive Data: User JWT. Staff user data from Authentication Service.
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowTask, WorkflowInstance, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowTaskReady). HTTP: Authentication Service (getStaffUserById, getDepartmentByCode/getUnitByCode). HTTP: Notification Service. Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger only. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. No visibility into REQUEST_INFO cycle duration or frequency.
Notes: Track time spent in REQUEST_INFO state to identify bottlenecks.

Description: Reassigns a task to a new user. Validates new assignee exists and has required role/dept/unit. Updates assignee, records ASSIGN history, emits WorkflowTaskReassigned, sends notification.
Criticality Reason: Reassignment changes who is responsible for an approval step. Incorrect reassignment to unauthorized users could bypass controls. Important audit trail requirement.
Important Log Fields: task_id, instance_id, old_assignee, new_assignee, reassigned_by, role_code, trace_id
Sensitive Data: User JWT. New assignee user ID. Staff user email for notification.
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowTask, WorkflowInstance, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowTaskReassigned). HTTP: Authentication Service (getStaffUserById). HTTP: Notification Service. Access Management Service (guard).
Existing Observability: NestJS Logger only. No SDK. No metrics. No tracing.
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Reassignment chains invisible.
Notes: Track reassignment frequency — high rates may indicate workload imbalance or role misconfiguration.

Description: Resumes all REQUEST_INFO tasks for an instance (those without requestInfo filter fields). Restores each task's state from history snapshot. Emits WorkflowTaskReady per resumed task. Sends notifications.
Criticality Reason: Bulk resume of paused tasks. Required to unblock workflows after clarification is provided. Failure leaves multiple tasks stuck.
Important Log Fields: instance_id, namespace, entity_ref, resumed_by, tasks_resumed_count, trace_id
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowInstance, WorkflowTask, WorkflowHistory. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowTaskReady). HTTP: Authentication Service. HTTP: Notification Service. Access Management Service (guard).
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics.

Description: Bulk task actions (APPROVE_ALL/REJECT_ALL). Maps to individual APPROVE/REJECT per task. Iterates calling actOnTask internally. Returns per-task results with success/failed/skipped counts. Each task NOT in single transaction — failures isolated.
Criticality Reason: Bulk approval/rejection. Processes multiple workflow tasks in one call. Partial failures possible. Used by staff to batch-process approval queues. High impact — can approve/reject multiple applications at once.
Important Log Fields: action (approve_all/reject_all), total_tasks, success_count, failed_count, skipped_count, failed_task_ids, actor_user_id, duration_ms, trace_id
Sensitive Data: User JWT. Per-task sensitive data same as actOnTask.
Dependencies: All deps of actOnTask multiplied by task count. Access Management Service (guard).
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Partial failure details invisible — no record of which tasks succeeded vs failed in a batch.
Notes: Critical — must log per-task results. Partial failures need clear visibility. Consider adding a bulk_action_id to correlate all individual task actions within one bulk request.

Description: Creates or returns immutable schema snapshot. Finds/creates WorkflowEntity, generates definition from steps payload, computes checksum, validates via Ajv, creates WorkflowSchema if new. Emits WorkflowSchemaCreated via outbox.
Criticality Reason: Defines the approval workflow structure. Incorrect schemas affect all future workflow instances. Schema immutability (checksum-based) provides safety. Failure prevents new workflow types from being configured.
Important Log Fields: schema_id, namespace, entity_type, schema_version, checksum, is_new_or_existing, step_count, created_by, trace_id
Dependencies: DB: Transaction — WorkflowEntity.findOne/create, WorkflowSchema.findOne/create. Kafka via outbox (WorkflowSchemaCreated). Access Management Service (guard).
Observability Gap: Zero structured logging. Zero metrics. Schema validation failures invisible.
Notes: Log schema validation failures (Ajv errors) prominently. Track new vs existing schema ratio.

Description: Fetches single task by PK. Parses payloadJson and roleCode. Returns null if not found (no 404).
Authentication: **PUBLIC — @Public() decorator bypasses AccessGuard. No authentication required.**
Criticality Reason: SECURITY CONCERN: Unauthenticated access to task data including assignee, roleCode, comment, fileUrl, departmentCode, unitCode, requestInfoRoleCode/DepartmentCode/UnitCode. Any person or bot can enumerate task IDs and read workflow data.
Sensitive Data: All task fields are publicly accessible: assignee ID, roleCode, comments, fileUrl, departmentCode, unitCode, requestInfo fields.
Dependencies: DB: WorkflowTask.findByPk.
Observability Gap: CRITICAL GAP: Unauthenticated endpoint with no access logging, no rate limiting, no metrics. Task data exposure is a security risk.
Notes: SECURITY: This endpoint is @Public() and exposes task data without authentication. Must be flagged to service owner. At minimum: add access logging with client IP, add rate limiting, consider whether this really needs to be public. If it does (e.g., for email links), consider adding a short-lived token parameter instead.
